summary: Wageningen University's Africa Scholarship Programme pays tuition, a living allowance, travel, visa and insurance for the full two years of a Wageningen MSc. It is for citizens of African countries with a First Class bachelor's degree and a GPA of 80% or higher. There is no form: Wageningen invites eligible applicants whose complete MSc application arrives before 1 December 2026.
meta_title: Wageningen Africa Scholarship Programme 2027: full MSc funding
meta_description: Wageningen's Africa Scholarship Programme covers tuition, living costs, travel and insurance for a two-year MSc. Apply for your MSc before 1 December 2026.
covers: Tuition fees for the 24 months of the MSc.
Travel to and from the Netherlands.
eligibility: A First Class honours bachelor's degree with a GPA of 80% or higher.
Unconditional admission to a Wageningen MSc programme that starts in September 2027. Every Wageningen MSc qualifies.
Preference goes to applicants who do not already hold a master's degree.
how_to_apply: There is no scholarship form. Apply for a Wageningen MSc that starts in September 2027 and submit the complete application before 1 December 2026.
Upload your bachelor's diploma and have your official English test results available before 1 December 2026.
Wageningen's scholarship committee assesses the applications that arrived in time and emails the selected applicants around March and April 2027.
A lottery among the selected applicants follows, and the scholarships are offered on 7 April 2027.
watch_out: Your bachelor's must be finished and uploaded before 1 December 2026, so final-year students cannot be considered this round.

Wageningen exempts only degrees taught in English on campus in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, the UK or the US (and some Dutch qualifications). An English-taught degree from Ghana, Nigeria or Kenya does not exempt you, so sit IELTS Academic (6.5 overall, speaking 6.0) or TOEFL iBT (90, speaking 22) in time for the results to exist before 1 December 2026.

The final choice is a lottery among the selected applicants, so apply for other funding too. Citizens of 64 developing countries are also considered for Wageningen's Anne van den Ban Fund through the same MSc application.
Wageningen's scholarships are for September starts only.
documents: A complete Wageningen MSc application, submitted before 1 December 2026
Your bachelor's diploma and transcripts, uploaded before 1 December 2026
Official IELTS or TOEFL results available before 1 December 2026

faq.q: Do I apply separately for the Africa Scholarship Programme?
faq.a: No. It is based on invitation. Submit a complete Wageningen MSc application before 1 December 2026 and meet the requirements to be considered.

faq.q: What grades does the Africa Scholarship Programme ask for?
faq.a: A First Class honours bachelor's degree with a GPA of 80% or higher.
Selected applicants are emailed around March and April 2027, and after a lottery the scholarships are offered on 7 April 2027.
